highlights.title: USA Today becomes the latest publisher to sue OpenAI
highlights.summary: USA Today Co., along with the several local newspapers it owns, is suing OpenAI over claims that the company copied "hundreds of thousands" of articles to train its AI models, as reported earlier by Reuters.
body: This is just the latest in a string of copyright lawsuits filed against OpenAI. In addition to a copyright lawsuit filed by The New York Times, OpenAI is also facing legal action from The Intercept, CNET owner Ziff Davis, CBC/Radio-Canada, Encyclopaedia Britannica, Merriam-Webster, The Seattle Times, and a coalition of nearly 400 local newspapers.

“OpenAI’s commercial success rests on large-scale copyright infringement,” USA Today Co.’s lawsuit claims. It alleges that OpenAI never asked for permission to use its content, instead “took” USA Today ’s content to “build products worth hundreds of billions of dollars.” The Tennessean, Indy Star, The Columbus Dispatch, The Oklahoman, and several other local outlets are also included in the lawsuit.

highlights.title: How Oracle turns days of work into minutes with ChatGPT and Codex
highlights.summary: Across recruiting, engineering, and operations, Oracle turns specialist knowledge into fast, repeatable workflows with ChatGPT Work and Codex.
body: Over a hundred thousand employees across Oracle are using ChatGPT Work and Codex, from talent acquisition to Oracle Applications Lab to the IT organization. In each case, work that used to rely on specialists and take days can now be done by anyone and is complete in minutes. Recruiters skip days of market research, business users describe an outcome instead of hunting for a report, and technical leads build tools that used to take a full team months.

The talent acquisition team used ChatGPT Work to build a talent market intelligence tool that takes a job description, researches comparable roles, benchmarks compensation, and assesses the talent pool across relevant locations. The tool arms the recruiter with valuable information that they need going into a conversation with the hiring manager, information that previously took 2–4 days to compile.

“We’ve gone from zero to a hundred,” says Jan Ackerman, Senior Vice President and Global Head of Talent Acquisition at Oracle. “Now we’re able to sit down and prep for about 15 to 20 minutes using the tool that we’ve built using [ChatGPT] Work.”

highlights.title: Hunter Bell celebrates in Team GB's 'glam' female track success
highlights.summary: Georgia Hunter Bell has enjoyed quite the year, winning a hat-trick of gold medals at the World Indoor Championships, for England at the Commonwealth Games, and again for Team GB at the European Championships.
body: But British female track success in 2025 certainly didn't stop there. Sprinter Amy Hunt made headlines with a record four-gold display in the Europeans in Birmingham, while Dina Asher-Smith now tops the all-time medal table at the championships after winning her 11th, eight of which are gold.

Among other successes, Keely Hodgkinson claimed World Indoor gold in the 800m in March - in the second-fastest indoor time in history - and set a new British record at that distance in the summer, though she'd be pipped to gold at the Europeans after sitting out the Commonwealth Games due to muscle tightness.
"It's really cool. just being part of this era. It's really fun," Hunter Bell told Sky Sports.
"We all know each other very well. We all travel together, see each other a lot throughout the year, so it's fun to tune in and be like, 'Oh, Amy's racing tonight'.

highlights.title: 'Exploring Pendola Pass' quest walkthrough in Arc Raiders
highlights.summary: The "Exploring Pendola Pass" quest in Arc Raiders is intended to be one of the first you tackle in the 'Frozen Trail' update, as it essentially acts as a whistlestop tour of some of the map's most notable points of interest.
body: Here's a full guide on how to complete "Exploring Pendola Pass" in Arc Raiders, including where to find the control room in Cielo Sereno Observatory and the tallest tower in the Railyard.

Destroying 20 Arc enemies is simple, if a little time-consuming, so we won't include a dedicated section for that one. I'd recommend using a long-range weapon, such as an Anvil or Renegade, to take out Wasps, Hornets, and Fireflies from afar, and steer clear of the new Bully enemy because it will absolutely ruin your day.

Make sure you have a wire on you when you visit the Railyard, and we recommend bringing a mobility gadget such as a grappling hook, snaphook, or zipline for both that task and the one at the observatory. Luckily, you receive three ziplines for accepting the quest, so make sure to bring them along.

The Cielo Sereno Observatory is located in the northeast corner of Pendola Pass. The quickest way to get to the control room (the location of which is shown in the image above) is to use a zipline, grappling hook, or snaphook to get on the roof. Otherwise, you can take the stairs underneath the building.

highlights.title: Trump administration says Microsoft ‘abused’ worker visa program and is cutting off access
highlights.summary: The Trump administration is suspending some tech companies, including Microsoft, from an immigration program that lets an employer hire foreign workers that can reside permanently in the US, as reported by Reuters.
body: Vice President JD Vance claims an immigration program used by tech companies has become ‘rife’ with fraud.

In a press conference, Vice President JD Vance claimed the permanent labor certification program — intended for use when there aren’t “sufficient” US workers available to do a job — has become “rife” with fraud over the “past several years,” and that no company has “abused” the system more than Microsoft. “Our message to Microsoft is: you’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers.”

The administration is also suspending companies including Adobe, Cognizant, and Infosys. Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling claims Microsoft and Adobe “requested almost 3 million foreign workers,” received “over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals,” and “over 100,000 permanent labor certifications.” Vance also said Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers last year and “benefited” from 6,300 H-1B visas and “almost 3,000 green cards.”

highlights.title: Are you ready for everything to look like TikTok?
highlights.summary: Since TikTok burst into mainstream consciousness, many things have been called a "TikTok clone": YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, Snapchat Spotlight, Netflix's Clips, LinkedIn's vertical video feed, and countless other, less recognizable names like Triller, Zynn, and Byte.
body: A pair of tests on Facebook and Instagram offer a preview of what all social media could come to look like.

For years now, Facebook and Instagram have pumped users’ feeds with video as Meta chases TikTok’s runaway success. But if tests running abroad are any indication, the TikTok-ification of social media might finally be reaching its fullest form.

TechCrunch reports that some users in India are getting a Facebook test that, upon opening the app, drops them directly into an immersive, full-screen video feed. Meta hinted that this “experience” would be coming to “video-heavy countries” first, followed by a potential US expansion in 2027. At the same time, Romania-based app researcher Radu Oncescu noticed an option on Instagram to have Reels be the first thing a user sees when they open the app. Instagram Stories remain at the top of the feed, per screenshots from Oncescu, while swiping the screen pulls up the traditional feed of posts from accounts a user follows. Sound is on for Reels by default.

Several reports on Thursday claim an agreement has been struck and that an announcement could be made as soon as next week to confirm Rwanda's addition to the calendar for the 2030 season.

Asked about the speculation ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix, Hamilton said: "I haven't really got any news for you. I saw something on people posting online, but I've always said that we need to have a Grand Prix in Africa.
"It is, for me, the most important continent, to be honest, the most beautiful continent. We're on all the other continents but that one and there should be no reason for it."

body: My Decoder guest today is Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, and we’re discussing the new wave of consumer-friendly AI agents.

Muse and Dots have had the highest-profile product launches, and they’re fascinating to pit against each other. Both Meta and OpenAI have decided to pitch these agents to mainstream users and businesses in the form of cute animated mascots.

These can do everything from the boring — restaurant reservations and inbox triage — to more sophisticated tasks. In OpenAI’s cases, the company is even offering “specialist” Dots for marketing, legal work, and accounting.

Muse, notably, is free, while Dots are not. So you’ll hear Hayden and me get into why Meta, which still doesn’t have a frontier model of its own, might have a meaningful edge here because it’s so much better at making and distributing consumer products.

highlights.title: Magic’s Most Versatile Mechanic Comes to Disney Lorcana With a Clever Twist
highlights.summary: Disney Lorcana is about to introduce its own version in the game’s fourth year. When Hyperia City arrives at local game stores on Oct. 16 for prerelease events ahead of the wider Oct. 23 launch, ink drops will also arrive as a new way to ramp up ink generation.
body: Few Magic: The Gathering mechanics have become as ubiquitous as Treasure tokens. These artifacts can be sacrificed to generate one mana of any color, which means that, regardless of the deck’s colors or strategies, they can help cast more expensive cards ahead of schedule. Or you can stockpile them for a single explosive turn. Treasure tokens have become so common and popular since their debut in 2017’s Ixalan block that they're now less of a specialized mechanic and more a fundamental part of how modern Magic works.

Having gotten hands-on with various Hyperia City cards provided by Ravensburger, however, I realized ink drops are more than Treasure tokens with a Lorcana makeover. Hyperia City distributes them across all six ink types (but not evenly). The most interesting cards don’t just generate extra resources. They reward each color for producing and spending ink drops in its own particular way. In particular, Hyperia City really wants you to combine two of those strategies into a deck focused on cards featuring characters from 1963’s The Sword in the Stone.

The film opens with a stunning shot of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Bridge, which will turn into a metaphor for building all-powerful AI systems over the course of the film. Again and again, Altman (played by Andrew Garfield) points to the bridge, first to convince his cofounder-to-be Ilya Sutskever (Yura Borisov) of the importance of their vision, then as a way to control the scientist.

Garfield is disturbingly riveting as Altman, with his hypnotizing performance painting the most damning picture of the OpenAI CEO yet in any form of media. He depicts Altman as a manipulative, power-hungry psychopath who lies as easily as he breathes and will use anyone, anytime, anywhere to get what he wants.

At one point, Hinton references a 2008 quote by Paul Graham, cofounder of Y Combinator, about Sam Altman: “You could parachute him into an island full of cannibals and come back in 5 years and he’d be the king.”

highlights.title: A good friend brings her dogs when she stays with me. I kind of dread it. What can I do? | Leading questions
highlights.summary: People often forget social rules when dogs are involved, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But you’ll have to say something if you want things to change. A good friend of mine stays with me regularly when she comes into town.
body: Eleanor says: It sounds as though you’re in the jam we all get into when we try to smooth things over: you can have the social ease of pretending something is fine; or the outcome from confessing it isn’t, but not both simultaneously.

Obviously, your friend should have paid more mind to the possibility that you don’t see her dogs like she does. Using the bathroom in your house? The first rule of society is that other people’s preferences might differ from yours, and that matters for how you treat them and their stuff.

But bring a dog into the equation and some otherwise intelligent people seem to forget that. They’ll trail behind on a leash giving the choreography of an apology while their dog puts paws on tables, bounds excitedly up to frightened children or treats furniture and food the way they’re allowed to at home. I’m saying this as a lifelong Dog Person, for what it’s worth: there is not a muddy paw print in the world I mind if it means I am playing with a dog. But we must admit, some dog people give the rest of us a bad name by assuming everyone sees their dog the way they do.

But you’ll have to say something if you want things to change.

However, Amazon shut down its app store last year. The new Alexa Tablets run full-fledged Google-y versions of Android with the Play Store and all the apps you'd expect. They run on the budget MediaTek 8189 processor, but that's still an upgrade from the last-gen Fire tablets. Both devices have 16:10 display ratios that are better for watching video, but the flagship tablet is a little different.

highlights.title: I spent years postponing my own joy. Here’s how I learned to say yes to the juicy bits of life | Sheree Joseph
highlights.summary: Society tells us there is one way to live a life, and joy is a byproduct on the path there. But you don’t need a reason to enjoy the act of being alive. I have been dwelling on what it means to live well. Not because I have mastered it, but because I have become very comically bad at it.
body: But most of all I became fixated on my fertility and how it dwindled in my early 30s, leaving me to make choices most women don’t have to until later. I tried to save my eggs and couldn’t. My lack of a partner in a conservative Catholic Lebanese family became a cudgel.
Pleasure was something bypassed on the way to a goal of being chosen and accepted. In other words, joy was a byproduct.
Trying to live well in a society that doesn’t prioritise it is like filling a cup with the bottom cut off: the water just runs through, passing you by, leaving you as parched as sandpaper.

A holiday was an opportunity to recover from work. In Italy, the plastic cup in my hand was solid and filled with the bitter strength of a negroni sbagliato – or a “broken negroni” – a drink whose name comes from the fact it was first made by mistake.
points: Society tells us there is one way to live a life, and joy is a byproduct on the path there.

body: The Nottingham Forest head coach said the league faces a job to repair its image and suggested supporters might switch off after City were found to have artificially inflated their income by more than £900m.

City have appealed against last week’s seismic judgment of an independent commission that they broke financial rules across a nine-year period. If City’s appeal fails, the panel could determine a range of sporting sanctions, including expulsion from the league and point deductions. Glasner said the case must be finalised “as soon as possible” to protect the competition’s integrity.

Glasner cited his experience of Crystal Palace being demoted from the Europa League at the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) last year for breaking Uefa’s multi-club ownership rules as an example of how legal processes can drag.

“Let’s wait until the final verdict is spoken, but my wish is just that this is quick,” Glasner said. “Because we didn’t know with Palace if we were in the Europa League or Conference League and then it was ‘you will hear on Thursday’ and then that became Monday, because it was always delayed. Then we got the final verdict 10 days before the Conference League started.
